The same test was run on all four sibling scales in this battery -- sj, kpnts, rwa and unjust -- and all four are stored PRE-RECODED, so this was a family-wide error in the first pass rather than a one-table slip. TRANSLATED COLUMN ADDED, AND ITS PROVENANCE IS MIXED PER ITEM -- 14 of the 16 English renderings were written by this project, so this table now carries IRW-GENERATED CONTENT and under the ruling of 2026-09-02 that requires a line on the public issues page. That entry does not exist yet and cannot be created from here; it is the one outstanding action on this row. WHY THE SUPPLIED LIST COULD NOT DO MORE, recorded so this is not retried the same way: it is the 14-item version of the scale, rated 'very negative (1) to very positive (7)', whereas this study administered the 16-item SDO6 on 1-5. Ten of its fourteen items have no counterpart in the administered set at all (including concept-rating entries like 'Increased economic equality' and 'Equality'), and three of the remaining four differ from the Polish in ways that matter: #7 reads 'step on others' where the Polish says other GROUPS, #9 is the noun phrase 'Increased social equality' where the Polish is a full sentence, and #11 adds 'in this country', which the Polish does not. Those three were therefore translated rather than borrowed. An earlier attempt using the SDO7 scale (Ho et al. 2015) was rejected for the same class of reason -- SDO7 dropped kpnts5's item entirely. The English that would settle this properly is Pratto, Sidanius, Stallworth & Malle (1994) Table 5, the 16-item SDO6 list, which was not retrievable here. TRANSLATION POLICY USED: rendered for meaning against the administered Polish rather than snapped to canonical SDO phrasing, so where the Polish diverges from the English original the translation follows the Polish. Two places that shows: kpnts7 and kpnts19 use 'better'/'worse' groups because the Polish reads lepsze/gorsze, where the canonical scale says superior/inferior; and kpnts22 is 'kept in check' for 'trzymane w ryzach'. Worth fixing upstream: the vocabulary offers a value that silently evades the check.

note: UPGRADED FROM THE FALLBACK: this table now ships the ADMINISTERED POLISH. It originally shipped English in the base fields as translated_substitute, on the finding that the Polish was in neither the deposit nor the paper. It is in neither -- but it IS in the Polish adaptation the paper cites, Grzesiak-Feldman (2012), whose Zalacznik 1 lists a 20-item 'Skala Prawicowego Autorytaryzmu'. All twelve items this study administered appear there verbatim. So Polish takes item_text, the .sav's English labels move to item_text_translated (the authors' own renderings, hence translation_source=study_supplied), and text_source becomes study_materials. THE PAIRING IS FORCED BY CONTENT, not position: each of the twelve English labels is a direct translation of exactly one numbered appendix item and vice versa, drawn from a pool of twenty. The map is rwa1<-13, rwa2<-2, rwa3<-8, rwa4<-4, rwa5<-9, rwa6<-1, rwa7<-14, rwa8<-7, rwa9<-12, rwa10<-6, rwa11<-11, rwa12<-3, so the study used appendix items 1-4, 6-9 and 11-14 and none of 5, 10 or 15-20. THE QUESTIONNAIRE ALTERNATED KEYING: the six items the appendix marks (R) land exactly on the odd codes rwa1, rwa3, rwa5, rwa7, rwa9, rwa11 -- the same alternating design the cons block shows, where odd items are one subscale and even the other. CORRECTS A CLAIM THIS TABLE ORIGINALLY SHIPPED. Its first public note said the items are 'stored RAW'. They are not. Solving for the weights of the deposit's own rwa_sum returns +1 on all twelve with a zero intercept, reproducing it for 342 of 342 complete rows; flipping the six reverse-worded items instead reproduces only 22 of 342. So the deposit stores them ALREADY RECODED, with higher meaning more authoritarian for every item. A consequence worth stating: keying polarity therefore cannot be used to test the pairing on this table -- all twelve intercorrelate positively, across-block r = +0.160 rather than negative -- and that is explained by the recoding rather than being a failure of the mapping. RESPONSE ANCHORS STILL NOT SHIPPED, and the new source is the reason to be careful rather than bolder: the appendix publishes a SIX-point scale ('(1) Zdecydowanie sie nie zgadzam' through '(6) Zdecydowanie sie zgadzam'), but this study administered FIVE points -- the paper says 5-point and the live data contains only 1-5. So the appendix's labels do not describe this administration and option_text stays blank. PROVENANCE CORRECTED -- text_source WAS study_materials AND IS NOW canonical_instrument, because the Polish shipped here is NOT established as the administered wording. Reading Radkiewicz (2011) properly shows the two are different Polish adaptations of RWA. Radkiewicz says of his own appendix: 'W badaniu zastosowano wersje zawierajaca 20 pozycji, wzorowana na tej, ktorej uzywal w swoich badaniach Duckitt' -- a 20-item version modelled on Duckitt, from Altemeyer's original. He cites Funke twice and Grzesiak-Feldman not at all. The lys study, by contrast, cites Funke (2005) adapted to Polish by Grzesiak-Feldman (2012), 12 items on three factors. So the appendix is an Altemeyer/Duckitt-lineage Polish RWA while the study administered a Funke-lineage one. WHAT IS STILL SOLID: the twelve items correspond in CONTENT, and that correspondence is not loose -- each of the .sav's twelve English labels is a direct translation of exactly one appendix item out of twenty, and independently the lys paper's own three RWA example items (one per factor) all appear in the appendix, as items 03, 02 and 04. Funke's 12-item scale is itself built from Altemeyer's pool, which is why the content overlaps. WHAT IS NOT SOLID: whether the Polish STRINGS are the ones respondents read. Grzesiak-Feldman's adaptation may word the same items differently, and her paper was not consulted. The close English-to-Polish fit is good evidence the two adaptations share wording, but it is evidence and not identity. NOTE THE RESULTING INVERSION, which is worth stating plainly: for this table the ENGLISH in item_text_translated is the more authoritative record of what was administered, because it comes from the study's own .sav, while the Polish in item_text is a published rendering of the same items from a sibling adaptation. Closing this needs Grzesiak-Feldman (2012) itself.

source_ref: Deposit workbook 'Knowledge and Fear of COVID-19 and Perceived Stress.xlsb' (osf.io/m2v3h) -- its 'Codebook' sheet keys Q1..Q12 to their statements and states '0 - Incorrect; 1 - Correct', its 'Survey 1' sheet carries the same twelve statements with the True/False answer key and a % Correct column, and its 'DataSet' sheet holds the response columns; data/kfcovid_Li2020/'knowledge and fear of covid_ knowledge scale.do' for the code derivation. Article: Li & Leung (2020), Data in Brief 33:106395, CC BY, PMC7546663.
note: BARE-INTEGER ITEM CODES THAT ARE NOT ACTUALLY OPAQUE. The live codes are 1-12, which normally demands reconstruction caution, but the .do file reshapes `Q1 Q2 ... Q12 -> Q` and renames the reshape index to `item`, so the integer IS the Q number; the Codebook sheet then keys each Q to its statement. The mapping is mechanical, not inferred. TWO SHEETS CROSS-CHECK EACH OTHER: the Codebook and Survey 1 statements are byte-identical for 11 of the 12, and the twelfth is recoverable only from Survey 1 because the Codebook's Q4 cell is a broken spreadsheet reference rendering as '0x17'. That item is 'Only those who are elderly, have chronic illnesses, and/ or are obese could suffer severe symptoms as a result of COVID-19.' EXTRACTION NOTE: the deposit is an Excel BINARY workbook (.xlsb), which openpyxl cannot read and no office converter was available; it was read positionally with pyxlsb. An earlier attempt that harvested UTF-16 strings out of the raw sheet bytes silently lost this same Q4 item, so the positional read matters. WHAT resp MEANS, and this is the thing a user must not misread: respondents chose among THREE options, 'True, false, I don't know', but the live table does not store that choice. It stores CORRECTNESS, 0 = Incorrect and 1 = Correct, per the Codebook sheet. So option_text labels the stored values and not what anyone selected, and correct_response is 1 for every item by construction. The substantive answer key, which is what the item is actually asserting, is: 1 - True; 2 - True; 3 - True; 4 - False; 5 - False; 6 - False; 7 - True; 8 - True; 9 - False; 10 - True; 11 - True; 12 - True. VERIFICATION: the workbook publishes % Correct per item, and the observed proportion of resp == 1 reproduces all twelve to 0.000e+00 -- see verify_kfcovid_Li2020.R. Instrument provenance: the article says the twelve were 'adapted from' Zhong et al. (2020), Int J Biol Sci 16:1745, so the wording shipped here is this study's own as deposited, not Zhong's. CORRECTION -- correct_response IS NOW BLANK, and was wrong to populate. It shipped as "1" for every item, on the reasoning that resp is correctness-coded so the correct response is trivially the one labelled Correct. That is defensible in the abstract and misleading in practice: on a TRUE/FALSE item, 'correct_response = 1' reads as 'the answer is True', which is false for items 4, 5, 6 and 9. @xingyi-zhang read it that way immediately, which is evidence enough that the field was doing harm. THE UNDERLYING DATA IS UNCHANGED AND WAS NOT WRONG: resp genuinely encodes correctness, not the answer, and that is now checked rather than asserted -- for each of the four False-keyed items the observed share of resp == 1 equals the workbook's published % Correct exactly (item 9, a False statement, shows 0.9909, which is its % correct; if resp were the literal answer it would show 0.0091). So the fix is to the presentation. correct_response is blank because this table's resp is a CORRECTNESS axis rather than an answer axis, so there is no key expressible against it; the substantive key sits in the public note where it cannot be mistaken for a resp value. THE KEY, for the record: items 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12 are TRUE statements; items 4, 5, 6 and 9 are FALSE statements. NOTE A SECOND VOCABULARY GAP, of the same shape as the translation_source one on the kpnts row: provenance_vocab.csv defines an empty key_source as 'the instrument has no correct answer (an attitude or frequency scale), so there is no key to source'. That is NOT this case -- the instrument has correct answers and the source publishes them; they simply cannot be expressed against a correctness-coded resp. The column is empty for want of a value that fits, and the reason is recorded here. FURTHER CORRECTION -- option_text IS NOW BLANK TOO, and for the same underlying reason as correct_response. It shipped as 'Incorrect' for resp 0 and 'Correct' for resp 1, taken from the workbook's Codebook sheet. But those are SCORING labels, not response options: the standard defines option_text as the 'literal text for a specific response option available for an item' and resp as the 'response value assigned to a specific option_text', and nobody could select 'Correct'. The options actually available were three -- 'True, false, I don't know' -- and this table does not store which was chosen. So this is precisely the case the standard's 'may legitimately be missing for behavior-scored items' clause covers, and both option_text and correct_response are blank. What remains, and what the table is for, is the twelve item wordings joined to the live codes. The administered options and the scoring labels are recorded here and in the public note rather than in the item columns, where they would misrepresent what resp is. REBUILT INTO THE raw_resp FORM, which is the third and correct answer to what this table's response columns should hold. History, because two earlier shapes were wrong and the reasons differ. First it shipped option_text = 'Incorrect'/'Correct' against resp 0/1 with correct_response = 1 -- wrong twice over: 'Correct' is a scoring label rather than an option anyone could select, and '1' on a true/false item reads as 'the answer is True', which is false for items 4, 5, 6 and 9. Then both fields were blanked as behavior-scored, which was honest but threw away real information: the administered options ARE published. The standard's raw_resp provision is what fits -- 'the item response data will have a scored response in the resp column ... while the item text will retain the categorical option in the resp_raw column'. So option_text and raw_resp now carry the three administered options verbatim from the workbook's Options column, 'True, false, I don't know'; resp is deliberately EMPTY, because the live resp is a scored 0/1 correctness value and three options cannot sit on a two-valued axis without making (item, resp) ambiguous; and correct_response now NAMES the correct option per item, which is what the schema intends and what makes the field meaningful instead of misleading. ONE PRECISION ABOUT WHY: validate_items describes this branch as 'scoring key not recoverable', which is NOT the reason here. The key is fully recoverable -- the workbook publishes a Correct Answer column, and it is transcribed into correct_response. The reason resp is empty is that the option-to-score mapping is MANY-TO-ONE: both 'false' and 'I don't know' score 0 on a True-keyed item. So this is a deliberate call, not a shortcut, and the gate's prompt to confirm that is answered here. CONSEQUENCE for a user: this item table no longer joins to the live data on resp, by design. The live 0/1 remains the scored correctness value and the itemtext side documents what respondents were actually offered. A casing note: the workbook's Options column reads 'false' lowercase while its Correct Answer column reads 'False' capitalised; correct_response is normalised to the option list's casing so that it joins to option_text.

note: SHIPPED PARTIAL: STRUCTURE WITHOUT WORDING. No item wording is published for this scale anywhere in the record, so item_text is blank for all twenty -- the .sav labels cons1..cons20 as bare strings 'conservatism item1'..'item20', and the CC BY paper reproduces exactly TWO of the twenty as unkeyed subscale examples: 'The Christian values should be specially protected in Poland.' (social) and 'Currently the richest people pay too high taxes.' (economic). Two of twenty, unkeyed, cannot be assigned to codes. WHAT IS SHIPPED INSTEAD is the subscale each item belongs to, and that is proven rather than inferred. The deposit scores cult_cons and ec_cons; solving for their weights over cons1..cons20 returns weights of exactly 1 on ten items and 0 on the other ten, with a zero intercept, reproducing both composites for all 385 complete rows to a maximum residual of 6.04e-14. THE SCALE ALTERNATES: the odd-numbered items are the cultural/social conservatism subscale and the even-numbered ones are economic conservatism, and the two sets partition all twenty with no overlap. Those are the two sections. Note the paper calls the first subscale 'social conservatism' while the deposit names its score variable cult_cons, 'cultural conservatism'; both names are recorded here because the source is not consistent. Note also that the paper says 'We included the social subscale in our analysis', so the published analysis used only the odd items, while this table carries all twenty. The response anchors are NOT shipped: the paper states a 5-point Likert scale but never its labels, and this block carries no value labels, so option_text is blank. The two blocks in the same battery that DO carry value labels (sj and kpnts) both read '1 = I totally disagree' through '5 = I totally agree', so this block plausibly used the same ladder, but that is an inference from a sibling block rather than anything the source states. Unblocking the wording needs the Wojciszke instrument itself, a Polish-language published questionnaire not carried in this deposit. Superseded this table's earlier blocked note. THE CITED SOURCE IS NOW IN HAND, AND IT DOES NOT PUBLISH THE ITEMS -- which makes this a settled block rather than an open search. The lys paper cites Radkiewicz (2011) for this instrument; that paper is 'Ile jest autorytaryzmu w prawicowym autorytaryzmie? Krytyka uzytecznosci narzedzia pomiaru', Psychologia Spoleczna 17:97-112, CEEOL id=108624. It carries exactly ONE appendix, ZALACZNIK 1, and that appendix is the Right-Wing Authoritarianism scale, not this instrument -- which is also why the 20-item Polish list circulating alongside this table belongs to lys_2020_rape_3_rwa and was used there. Radkiewicz describes the Wojciszke instrument in prose only: 'Narzedzie autorstwa Wojciszke zbudowane jest z dwoch podskal (kazda wskaznikowana przez 10 pozycji)', with reliabilities alpha = 0.82 for the worldview subscale and 0.75 for the economic one. INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION OF THE SHIPPED STRUCTURE: 'each indicated by 10 items' is exactly the 10/10 split solved from the deposit's cult_cons and ec_cons scores, arrived at from the data with no knowledge of this sentence. SUBSCALE NAMING, three names for the same thing, recorded because the sources disagree: Radkiewicz calls it swiatopogladowa (worldview), the deposit names its score variable cult_cons (cultural), and the lys paper calls it social conservatism. SIX EXAMPLE ITEMS are published, three per subscale, still unkeyed to codes. Worldview: 'Wartosci chrzescijanskie powinny byc w Polsce szczegolnie chronione' (Christian values should be specially protected in Poland); 'Polska powinna byc przede wszystkim dla Polakow' (Poland should be first and foremost for Poles); 'Zycie poczete powinno podlegac bezwzglednej ochronie prawnej' (Conceived life should be under absolute legal protection). THAT LAST DETAIL CORROBORATES THE FAMILY-WIDE RECODING FINDING: the economic subscale contains reverse-coded items, yet ec_cons is reproduced by a PLAIN sum of the ten even items for all 385 rows, so this block is stored pre-recoded like its four siblings. Radkiewicz cites it without a printed appendix, so six of twenty is the ceiling from the cited source and no retry against Radkiewicz will do better.
